Dcoop (Jaen): cooperative production and storage data; 300,000 MT capacity
MAPA: Spanish olive oil production and area statistics 2024
IOC: Spain export price EUR 3.22/kg vs Italy EUR 4.42/kg (2023/24)

_meta.note: N-D-C values derived from PDI_andalucia_olive_20260606.yaml using formulas: balance=100-(|D-C|/max(D,C))*100; N=sqrt(D*C)*(balance/100); sustainability=100/((|D-C|^2)+10). All values PROVISIONAL pending field data collection. Paired comparison system: see PDI_marina_alta_20260606.yaml.

synthetic.label: Synthetic Baseline
synthetic.description: Baseline N-D-C values derived from PDI research data and public sources. Paired with Marina Alta ecosystem for comparative analysis. See _meta.sources for citations.

phase_meta.name: Ecosystem Baseline
phase_meta.transformation: Precipitation + solar energy -> degraded soil biological capital (Guadalquivir watershed; 50-100 T/ha/yr erosion in Jaen)

phase_meta.name: Agricultural Production
phase_meta.transformation: Monoculture inputs + irrigation -> maturing olives on tree (herbicide bare-soil management)

phase_meta.name: Harvest
phase_meta.transformation: Ripe olives on tree -> bulk bins delivered to mill (mechanised shakers; 90% mechanisation rate)

phase_meta.name: Primary Processing
phase_meta.transformation: Olives in bulk bins -> EVOO in tank (Dcoop-scale cooperative mills; 1,750+ mills Andalucia)

phase_meta.name: Quality Certification
phase_meta.transformation: Bulk EVOO -> DOP/IGP certified product (only 8% of production) or uncertified commodity bulk (92%)

phase_meta.name: Market Distribution and Trade
phase_meta.transformation: Bulk EVOO -> export revenue at EUR 3.22/kg average (67% bulk; EUR 890M foregone vs Italian bottling premium)

phase_meta.name: Regenerative Transition
phase_meta.transformation: Conventional monoculture -> cover-cropped biodiversity-enhanced grove (Danyadara; Olivares Vivos; sub-5% penetration)

phase_meta.name: Ecosystem Restoration
phase_meta.transformation: Eroded slopes + degraded Guadalquivir watershed -> stabilised soils + biodiversity recovery (nascent; no national programme at scale)

0.notes: Primary structural failure: soil biology severely degraded by 40+ years bare-soil herbicide management; erosion 50-100 T/ha/yr; no high-recharge aquifer system; Guadalquivir at 2.5 km3 annual deficit.

soil_organic_matter_pct.source: Olivares Vivos / Univ. Jaen monitoring data

biodiversity_deficit_pct.unit: % fewer bird species vs polyculture reference

0.scope_source: Ecosystem baseline carbon data requires dedicated soil survey: not yet available at regional scale

1.notes: Monoculture production is efficient (irrigation + fertiliser inputs well-managed) but structurally dependent on external inputs due to absent soil biology. Water stress increasing annually.
1.scope_source: Agricultural inputs emissions require per-farm survey: not provided

2.notes: Mechanised harvest is Andalucia's operational strength: 90% mechanisation rate, 80% labour cost reduction vs manual picking. Trade-off: bruising reduces polyphenol content and premium grade ceiling.

mechanisation_rate_pct.unit: % (Jaen and Cordoba; lower in mountain zones)

2.scope_source: Harvest machinery fuel emissions data not aggregated

3.notes: Best-managed phase: Dcoop-scale cooperative mills are among the world's most efficient; extraction rates 18-22%; modern two-phase decanters. Limitation: bulk mixing prevents traceability.
3.scope_source: Mill energy consumption data not aggregated at Andalucia regional level

4.notes: Certification gap: only 8% of production certified DOP/IGP despite 12 active designations. Cooperative bulk mixing destroys traceability. Olivares Vivos biodiversity certification covers only 12,000 of 1.8M ha.

dop_designations_andalucia.source: MAPA / Foods and Wines from Spain

4.scope_source: Certification level emissions boundary not relevant at this phase

5.notes: Primary downstream bottleneck: EUR 1.20/kg price gap vs Italy; EUR 890M annual foregone brand premium; 67% bulk export. Same balance as Phase 0: twin structural failures at opposite ends of the chain.
5.scope_source: Logistics and transport emissions not aggregated at export chain level

6.notes: Regenerative transition: programmes exist (Danyadara, Olivares Vivos, Regen Academy) but sub-5% grove penetration. No financial instrument to bridge the year-one yield-drop barrier.

danyadara_methodology.value: Syntropic agroforestry; water retention earthworks; food forest in olive groves

cover_crop_moisture_retention_gain_pct.source: Danyadara field data; Olivares Vivos monitoring

transition_yield_drop_year_1_pct.source: Regen Academy Spain / Danyadara practitioner data

6.scope_source: Transition phase carbon sequestration potential not yet measured at programme scale

7.notes: Ecosystem restoration at landscape scale: no national programme; Guadalquivir underfunded; Olivares Vivos 2030 target of 100,000 ha (current 12,000 ha, 0.7% of Andalucia grove area). Lowest balance; most opaque.

olivares_vivos_2030_target_ha.unit: ha (current: 12,000 ha; 0.7% of Andalucia grove area)

restoration_funding_available.value: No dedicated national programme at scale

eu_soil_strategy_2030_status.value: Framework exists; implementation regulations not yet operationalised for olive landscapes

7.scope_source: Ecosystem restoration carbon sequestration potential requires landscape-scale monitoring programme

synthetic.interpretation: Twin structural failures at Phase 0 (Ecosystem Baseline, 65.4%) and Phase 5 (Market/Trade, 65.3%). Andalucia is operationally efficient in harvest and processing (Phases 2-3) but failing at ecosystem foundation and value capture. System average balance 75.9% vs Marina Alta 86.3%.
